iut_type: USD wire transfer proxy service for Bluetooth SIG Declaration fee -- exchange rate timing and delegation pros/cons
customer_question: If we delegate the USD wire transfer for the SIG registration fee to your company, when exactly does the exchange rate get fixed? Also, what are the pros and cons of having you handle the wire transfer versus doing it ourselves?
question_variants: Is the exchange rate locked in at the time of formal quote issuance, or at some other point?
Why would a customer choose to pay the extra fee for transfer delegation instead of just wiring the funds directly themselves?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to understand exactly how the exchange rate would be determined if they delegated the USD wire transfer to the consultant, and wanted a clear comparison of when delegation makes sense versus handling the transfer themselves.
plain_english_explanation: When the wire transfer is delegated, the exchange rate applied is the TTS (telegraphic transfer selling) rate as of the last business day of the month prior to the formal quotation being issued -- a fixed reference point rather than a rate determined at the time funds are actually sent. As for why customers choose delegation despite directly paying themselves being the generally recommended default: common reasons include wanting to consolidate the SIG fee with the consultant's own support fees into a single internal billing/accounting entry, or facing internal accounting constraints that prevent a fast USD wire transfer. Delegation costs an additional ¥100,000 fee and takes about 3 weeks to complete, which customers should weigh against their own banking capability and internal process convenience.
consultant_answer: If you delegate the wire transfer to us, the exchange rate applied is the TTS rate as of the last business day of the month before the formal quote is issued -- a fixed reference point, not the rate on the day funds are actually sent. We generally recommend customers pay the SIG fee directly themselves, but delegation is popular among customers who want to consolidate billing with our own fees into one internal entry, or whose accounting department can't quickly process a USD wire transfer. Delegation costs an additional ¥100,000 and takes about 3 weeks.
decision_logic: When a customer asks about delegating the SIG Declaration fee wire transfer, clarify the exact exchange rate reference point (TTS rate, fixed at the prior month's last business day relative to quote issuance) and present the genuine tradeoffs (cost and lead time vs. billing consolidation or internal accounting constraints) rather than simply stating a preference for self-payment.
final_recommendation: When discussing wire transfer delegation, always state the specific exchange rate timing rule explicitly, since 'the rate at transfer time' is a reasonable but incorrect assumption a customer might otherwise make, and present the real-world reasons other customers have chosen delegation so the current customer can weigh their own situation against it.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer assuming the exchange rate would be fixed at the time of actual fund transfer, rather than the prior-month TTS rate tied to quote issuance, could be surprised by a different final cost than expected.
